reader: Claude Opus 5.5, research reader with source access
reason: The first reading of the faded, heavily abbreviated hand left many gaps and misread words, which were filled and corrected on contrast-enhanced images with the edition in hand.
sources: S. Thomae Aquinatis Opera omnia, Parma, vol. 23, Expositio I in Apocalypsim, cap. 16, pp. 467 (scan n478), 468 (scan n479), 470 (scan n481), Internet Archive sanctithomaeaqui23thom
R. E. Lerner, 'Poverty, Preaching, and Eschatology in the Revelation Commentaries of "Hugh of St Cher"', Studies in Church History Subsidia (abstract only consulted)
text:
Source-assisted reading of F-cf1m (Stams, Frg. 92), made with the Parma edition (vol. 23, Expositio I in Apocalypsim) in hand. Reread on the images: canvas 1, right page, col. a, lines 1-12 and col. b, lines 1-13; canvas 0, left page, col. b, lines 1-8 (contrast-enhanced); canvas 0, right page, col. b, lines 4-9 (contrast-enhanced); canvas 1, right page, col. a, lower half (read first without the source by an independent checker, two lines rechecked afterwards). Expansions in parentheses; (?) uncertain; [ ] lost or supplied. Native-pixel boxes are x0,y0,x1,y1.

Canvas 1 (Stams_STA_Frg_092_01v), right page, col. a, box 4080,1400,4900,2150:
1 [...] (torn)
2 avaru(m) cui(us) d(omi)n(u)s dives(?) (et) largus e(st)
3 talis e(st) o(mn)is avarus (et) io(deo) ab o(mn)ib(us) e(st)
4 maledict(us). Io(deo) d(icit) Ecc(lesiastic)i x. Avaro n(ichi)l
5 e(st) scelestius. Ib(ide)m: Nich(il) e(st) iniqui(us)
6 q(uam) amare pecunia(m). Hic e(nim) (et) a(n)i(m)a(m)
7 sua(m) venalem. Venalem h(abe)t q(uonia)m in vita
8 sua p(ro)iecit intima sua. Un(de) aranee
9 co(m)p(ar)at(ur) avarus quia sicut aranea
10 eviscerat se ut telu(m) texat sic avarus.
11 Un(de) Ysa(ie) lix. Co(n)fidu(n)t in nichilu(m) (et)
12 [lo]quu(n)tur vanitate(m) co(n)ceperu(n)t dolore(m) ...

Canvas 1, right page, col. a, lower half, box 3980,2130,4880,3260 (independent checker's reading, corrected on the image after the source):
(et) peperer(un)t iniquitate(m). Ova aspidu(m) ruper(un)t (et) telas aranee texer(un)t. (et) tele eor(um) n(on) erunt in vestim(en)t(um) neq(ue) operie(n)t(ur) op(er)ib(us) suis. op(er)a e(nim) illor(um) inutilia. Io(deo) [...] v(e) filii desertores [...] ut faceretis co(n)siliu(m) (et) n(on) ex [me] [...] tela(m) (et) n(on) p(er) sp(iritu)m meu(m). [...] su(m)mu(m) malu(m) avaricie [...] -latr- [...] ap(osto)l(u)s ad Ephe(sios) avaricia q(ue) e(st) ydolor(um) s(er)vitus [...] e(st) d(eu)m negare [...] fugiat [...] phiola(?) effu(n)d- [...] [quae]dam mala que ip(s)a facit o(mn)ib(us) h(ab)entib(us)

1 [...] multa horrea(?) p(re)paraverat magn[a]
2 (et) lata ubi posset reponere o(mn)ia
3 sua s(cilicet) paup(er)es q(ui) c(um) multo incremento(?) o(mn)ia
4 redderent t(em)p(or)e oportuno. Io(deo) d(icit) Ecc(lesiast)es ii
5 de divite: Quid p(ro)derit ho(min)i de univ(er)so(?) ...
6 labore s(uo) (et) afflictione sp(iritu)s q(ua) sub sole cruciat(us)
7 e(st). Cu(n)cti dies ei(us) laborib(us) (et) er(umnis)
8 pleni sunt nec p(er) nocte(m) mens quiescit.
9 Ecc(lesiast)e v. Saturitas aut(em) divit(is)
10 n(on) sinit eu(m) dormire. S(ecundu)m malu(m) e(st) turbac(i)o
11 cordis (et) tocius domus. Un(de) Prov. xv.
12 Conturbat domu(m) sua(m) q(ui) sectat(ur) avari-
13 cia(m). [...]

Postea; residens neq(ue) illa; nob(is) ... misere(re)(?) anime tue(?). Upper turn-in above this page: De confessione.
